verdicts.reason: The kernel estimates prove Nf is C^1, and the bounded inner-region and Taylor errors justify the divergent second-derivative difference quotient at zero. The continuous compactly supported source therefore gives Nf not C^2.

The explicit mild solution has unequal one-sided derivatives at the interior jump, so classicality fails. Dependency restatements and the Dini sufficiency estimate are consistent with the supplied interfaces; no fatal defect found.

The measurable witness has support in Q, satisfies the required size bound and zero moment, and takes opposite nonzero values arbitrarily close to every interior point of the cutting slice. The dependency restatements and the n=1 case are valid.

The cube containment and volume estimate are correct, and their lower bound diverges. Monotone convergence then proves global nonintegrability; BMO membership is accurately supplied by the cited dependency.

The cutoff approximation proves H^1_0 membership, the forcing is smooth and in L^2, and the divergent radial Hessian integral excludes H^2. Dependency restatements and the Lipschitz sector geometry are consistent.

The cutoff approximation establishes H¹₀ membership, the weak equation holds, and the explicit Hessian yields the stated sharp divergence threshold. The elementary polar and cutoff facts are standard, and the example respects the a priori estimate’s scope.

The piecewise linear function lies in H^1 and has constant flux au'=1, so it solves the weak equation with f=0. Its first derivative jumps at 0, giving u''=-δ₀/2 and excluding H²_loc. The dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces.

Both sequences lie in the prescribed faces and converge to (0,0); continuity forces u(0,0)=1 and u(0,0)=0. The dependency restatements are accurate, and the corner obstruction holds independently of the heat equation.

The jump's positive Kruzhkov entropy production is correctly computed. The composite profile satisfies the weak equation, entropy inequalities and initial trace; its concave-hull description and all dependency uses are consistent.

The regularity and energy argument correctly identifies the one-dimensional kernel. The supplied Fredholm interface then gives exactly the stated orthogonality condition, nonexistence for f=sin(kx), and nonuniqueness whenever a solution exists.

The quadratic expansion correctly gives stationarity; testing with u and applying Poincare proves uniqueness. A nonzero compactly supported bump yields arbitrarily negative values and smaller values arbitrarily near zero. Dependency restatements are consistent.

The witness is smooth, satisfies u_t−Δu>0, and has cylinder maximum e^T>1 versus parabolic-boundary maximum 1. Dependency restatements and the exclusion of (π/2,T) match the supplied interfaces; applying the maximum principle to −u is consistent.

All four witnesses are valid. The formula applications, strict integral signs, nonsmoothing profile, and regularity through time zero are justified and consistent with the supplied dependency interfaces.

The piecewise constant function lies in H^1(Ω), has zero weak gradient, and has supremum 1 and infimum 0. This refutes the comparison; the local Harnack and finite-chain interfaces are accurately qualified.

The smooth nonnegative polynomial satisfies -Δu=-1 and has zero infimum but positive supremum and L^p norm. It refutes both forcing-free comparisons; the cited additive estimates and dimension restrictions are used consistently.

Both conjugates are computed correctly. The nonconvex example violates the viscosity subsolution inequality, while the nonsuperlinear example has the stated restricted Lagrangian domain. Dependency restatements and scope are accurate.

The rescaled bumps are bounded in W^{1,p} and converge uniformly to zero, while their endpoint Hölder seminorms remain at least 1. Any Hölder-convergent subsequence would therefore give a contradiction; the dependency interfaces are consistent.

The cited ACL and reflexivity interfaces justify Sobolev membership and weak convergence. The computed energies refute weak sequential lower semicontinuity; nonconvexity and the existence-theorem caveats are correct.

The continuous representative of any admissible v would be at least 1 at both endpoints, contradicting its zero trace. The supplied trace-truncation interface also licenses the general necessity of boundary compatibility on the interval.

The ACL argument and polar estimates establish the witness in H^1. Changing its value at the Lebesgue-null origin changes the Dirac pairing, proving representative dependence. The cited interfaces support the argument.

The locally constant indicator has zero weak gradient and global mean 1/2, giving strictly positive oscillation norm for every 1≤p<∞. The cited interfaces and choice hypotheses support the counterexample and John-domain comparison.

The dependency restatements are accurate. Translation preserves the Sobolev norm, and every subsequence contains arbitrarily separated indices with fixed positive L^p distance, so no subsequence converges.

The inverse-transform formula, harmonic-series lower bound, and dilation identity are valid under the cited interfaces. They establish that every sharp-cutoff kernel has infinite L1 norm, refuting the asserted uniform bound.
The vertex shift, closedness-based domain induction, and Hölder forcing estimate are valid and match the dependency interfaces. The unused compatibility tower causes no defect.

The cone-distance inequality excludes the source and initial data from every backward cone outside the expanded compact set. Finite propagation gives pointwise vanishing; closedness yields the support inclusion. Empty K and t=0 are handled correctly.

The proof steps and dependency restatements are valid for the principal Dirichlet form. Generation, decay, domain identifications and smoothing follow with the stated choice assumptions and boundary compatibility conditions; no fatal defect found.

Sharp energy conservation and continuity force the density, hence all space-time derivatives, to vanish. Convexity gives a single constant, identified by the Cauchy limits. The zero-energy equivalence and difference argument are valid; dependency restatements are accurate.

The doubling argument correctly makes u-v a subsolution of w_t-L|Dw|=0. The smooth cone barrier has the required sign and initial order; comparison applies via semicontinuity at t=0. The strict cone and equality clause follow.

The interval Lipschitz bound satisfies the local theorem's hypotheses. A countable exhaustion and monotone convergence give global contraction almost everywhere; local L1 continuity extends the bound to every time, including endpoints.

The translation is bijective and preserves the Lagrangian term, so taking infima yields the stated two-sided modulus bound. Dependency restatements are accurate, and the t=0 case and uniform spatial equicontinuity follow.

The compactness–contradiction argument is valid. The supplied extension theorem applies at k=1, all Rellich branches yield L^p convergence, and the a priori estimate gives convergence in the closed Dirichlet space. No fatal interface inconsistency found.

The assumed moments justify continuous Fourier derivatives by dominated convergence. Peano Taylor expansion contradicts the cited little-o decay for every nonzero derivative through order s, including the integer endpoint. Dependency use and interfaces are consistent.

Constant solutions and the cited comparison principle give the range bound. The signed extrema argument, Fubini passage to slices, and local L1 continuity extension are valid and consistent with the supplied dependency interfaces.

Two-sided variations are admissible on compact subsets of {u>psi}; cutoffs and Radon inner regularity establish its measure zero. Continuity upgrades the obstacle inequality to pointwise order, yielding contact-set concentration and the zero integral. Dependencies match.

The segment estimate, affine substitutions, mean bound, local mollification and exhaustion limit are valid for real and complex scalars, including p=1. The cited interfaces support the argument, and the stated dimension-only constant follows.

The local weak-solution definition supplies uniform ellipticity. Restriction to compact interior patches licenses every regularity estimate; the embedding and one-dimensional arguments give compatible smooth representatives, and continuity upgrades the equation to pointwise equal

The expansion and Lax–Milgram identity give J(v)-J(u)≥(α/2)‖v-u‖², proving strict minimality without using uniqueness. Dependency restatements, scalar conventions, and the zero-space case are consistent.

The relaxed initial conditions justify the semicontinuous extensions; comparison applies to both envelope pairs. Constant shifts preserve the equation, yielding uniqueness and the stated sup-norm contraction. Dependency restatements are accurate.

The exponent inequalities correctly invoke the supplied embedding interface, the ball witness rules out C^{2,alpha} representatives, and the L^p/distributional equality argument is valid. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The definitions and dependency restatements are consistent. Cube averages are finite by containment in a ball; cube containment proves the factor 2^n comparison, and standard ball–cube inclusions give dimensional comparability.

The average inequalities, seminorm laws, characterization of zero oscillation, and cube/ball comparison are valid. The quotient is consistent with the supplied convention allowing L1_loc to denote almost-everywhere classes.

The definitions are coherent under the stated graph-continuous meaning of strong solution. The cited integration results support continuity and the classical–strong equivalence for continuously extended forcing; endpoint and mild-solution caveats are consistent.

Local boundedness makes the envelopes real-valued, localization licenses the cited envelope properties, and the two relaxed initial conditions force continuous attainment of the datum. The viscosity inequalities and envelope roles match the supplied interfaces.

P_N is a finite seminorm on Schwartz space; dilations make every convolution well-defined, including zero-integral tests. The class inclusion and resulting monotonicity are correct and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The norm definitions, scaled-ball dependency restatement, dilation identity, boundary-extension argument and examples are mathematically consistent. No fatal defect or conflict with the supplied interfaces was found.

The definition is coherent: bounded cube support and the a.e. size bound ensure absolute convergence of all moments. The prescribed order, threshold intervals, representative caveat, and ball-to-cube normalization are consistent with the supplied interfaces.
The Banach-space extension is explicit and sound. The one-sided limit defines a unique operator, and the domain and linearity arguments follow from the cited interfaces. No fatal defect found.

The domain, convolution compatibility, rescaling, support bounds, companion identity and low-frequency integrals are valid. The L2 norm bound follows from the cited multiplier theorem and agreement on the Schwartz core.

The zero-extension argument, density equivalences, restriction property, and fixed-L² comparison with zero-boundary Dirichlet solutions are valid under the supplied interfaces. The global H¹ requirement is an explicit convention.

The cited inequalities establish absolute convergence and joint continuity, Tonelli defines the nonnegative cone integral, and Fatou proves lower semicontinuity. Representative independence and endpoint cases are valid; no fatal defect found.

The definitions, positivity and integrability conclusions, A_1 infimum attainment, maximal-function comparisons, and invariance claims are valid and consistent with the supplied dependency interfaces.

The binary-digit formula is well-defined, gives the stated alternating signs on dyadic intervals, and yields Borel measurable, integrable functions with zero mean. The cited interfaces support the measure and integral calculations under Countable Choice.

The defining identity, closedness argument, equivalence with Lu=λu, and reality of eigenvalues are valid under the supplied symmetric-form interface. Class conventions and arbitrary-open-domain caveats are consistent.

The cited derivative interface uses coordinate indices 0,...,n−1, but L sums over 1,...,n without defining a relabelling. Thus ∂_n is undefined under that interface, already when n=1, and the operator is not well typed.

The densities, spatial flux and extended total energy are well-defined under the stated hypotheses. The sign and speed conventions agree with the supplied local conservation law and total-energy interfaces.

The definition is well typed: the form and H^{-1} pairing are conjugate-linear in the test function, g belongs to the trace's L^2 target, and the cited interfaces justify representative independence and absolute convergence.

The representative modification, measure regularity and null-set equivalence, and real and complex L^p completeness are valid. The cited dependency interfaces support the claims; no fatal defect found.

The measurable half-cube difference has support in the closed cube, the required size bound and zero integral. The uniform H^1 estimate follows from the cited atom lemma with p=1, s=0 and the stipulated admissible order.

The character parametrisation, compact-open topology argument, quotient factorisation and inverse-transpose annihilator formula are sound. The computations cover n=0 and k=0,n and agree with the supplied dependency and A/B interfaces.

The cited regularity theorem applies at every order; local Sobolev representatives glue uniquely, including in dimension one, and continuity upgrades the almost-everywhere equation to a pointwise identity. All essential dependency hypotheses are satisfied.

The solver applies to the strictly convex Burgers flux; the speed calculation, entropy admissibility, Lax inequalities and uniform local L1 trace bound are correct and consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The computations correctly establish sesquilinearity and coercivity of a, failure of both conditions for b, and the zero-form exception. Dependency restatements and applicability claims agree with the supplied interfaces.

The classical verification, upper-contact gradient bound, impossibility of lower contact at the centre, and boundary-distance calculation are correct for every n≥1 and consistent with the supplied interfaces.
The title promises a ridge point, but u(x)=|x| has a strict minimum at 0—a tip, not a ridge. The proof establishes the claimed tip behavior but supplies no ridge-point example.

The recursion correctly reduces to j=1 and gives mθ(0)=2. All dependency restatements agree with their interfaces; only θ has vanishing recursion coefficient among actual weights, consistently with the supplied A/B interfaces.

The A2 Weyl lengths and dot-action weights are correct. Kostant's theorem applies to the dominant integral weight 0 and yields the stated dimensions, distinct weights, and vanishing above degree 3; no fatal defect found.

The drift has zero real diagonal part by density, preserving the stated coercivity. The radial bump correctly yields a nonzero symmetry defect. Boundedness, Lax–Milgram applicability, and dependency restatements are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

Scaling gives the claimed norms and Sobolev membership. Hölder, dominated convergence and duality prove weak convergence, while unit norms exclude every strongly convergent subsequence, including when p=1.

The inverse action on a normalized eigenfunction gives the stated lower bound; the cited norm formula and discreteness justify blow-up near each eigenvalue. Dependency restatements and the resolvent sign convention are consistent.

The resolvent geometry, essential-range spectrum proof, adjoint calculation, and exponential semigroup construction are sound. The dependency interfaces and conditional nonselfadjointness claim are consistent.

The dependency interfaces license degree -1, the projective-line vanishing, and the self wall-crossing isomorphisms. Both arguments correctly force all cohomology to vanish, with consistent hypotheses and conventions.

Poisson's formula applies to the stated data. For t>r/c the support lies strictly inside the integration disk, and the positive kernel with continuous nonnegative, nonzero data gives u(x0,t)>0. Dependency restatements and the three-dimensional contrast are consistent.

The ball–cube comparisons and countable rational-cube argument establish both implications and the dimensional bounds. Dependency restatements are accurate, and zero essential infima and almost-everywhere exceptions are handled correctly.

Hölder yields the stated comparison with the correct A_p constant; the A_1 bound follows from the supplied essential-infimum interface. The indicator and complement arguments and local-integrability conclusion are valid, including infinite-integral cases.

The line restriction is C² by the cited calculus rules. Fermat gives φ′(0)=0; Taylor's Lagrange remainder and continuity of φ″ imply D²F(u)[v,v]≥0. Domain, interiority, and the zero direction are handled correctly.

The trace and kernel interfaces license every step: the fiber is a nonempty translate of W_0^{1,p}, is convex and norm closed, and hence weakly closed. The translate identity uses only TRg=g, so it holds for every stated right inverse.
The truncation argument, Hölder tail estimates, closedness passage and endpoint continuity are sound. Dependency restatements and graph-norm conclusions are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The range-density argument, symmetry calculation and lower bounds follow from the supplied interfaces. Dependency restatements are accurate in the symmetric setting, and the proof also covers empty and unbounded open sets without boundary regularity.

Uniform step approximations establish strong measurability and Bochner integrability. Linearity and the norm inequality yield both average estimates, and continuity at t forces their errors to zero. The dependency interfaces and endpoint cases are consistent.

The geometric inclusions, volume ratios, integral comparisons, and characteristic bounds are valid. The supplied cube interface also licenses comparison of centred and uncentred operators, yielding the stated boundedness equivalence.

The polar-coordinate calculation, continuity argument, and differentiation are valid for continuous real data and every n≥1, r>0. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces; no fatal defect found.

The enclosing-cube construction, telescoping estimates, and logarithmic bound are valid. Local dependency restatements follow from the supplied interfaces, including for complex-valued BMO functions; the case Q=R is handled.

The graph construction, two-sided Hölder norm estimates, chain-rule coefficient formulas and ellipticity bounds are sound. Dependency restatements and the supplied A/B interfaces are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The kernel estimates, spherical cancellation, boundary correction sign, Hölder formula and distributional truncation argument are valid. Dependency hypotheses are met, and the Lipschitz endpoint asserts only C² regularity, consistently with the A/B interfaces.

The atomic characterisation supplies an atomic representation converging in H1, and norm convergence yields the required finite approximation. The dependency restatements, p=1 specialisation, reindexing and tail bound are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The restriction is bounded by the cited embedding, complex Riesz representation is used with the correct conjugation, and the mean-zero test proves nested compatibility. Countable gluing and uniqueness up to an almost-everywhere additive constant are valid.

The iterated chain rule and multinomial weight estimate establish the stated seminorm bound; continuity and the inverse follow. Dependency restatements and relevant A/B interfaces are consistent, and the argument requires no choice.

The translation substitution, polarization identity, and approximate-identity density argument are valid. Dependency restatements match the supplied interfaces, and the core agrees with the dual-normalisation interface without assuming inversion prematurely.

Fourier–Stieltjes uniqueness forces q to vanish locally; the countable compact exhaustion resolves the varying null sets. Completeness then gives surjectivity and hence dense range. The level-set formulas are understood for n≥1.

The proof correctly handles non-sigma-finite Haar measure, translation continuity, symmetric normalised kernels, and uniform approximate-identity convergence. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent.

The closure argument is valid even for nonabelian groups; the dependency restatements are accurate. The converse follows by intersecting compact neighbourhoods with the closed subgroup. No choice or A/B-interface conflict arises.

The finite ancestor chain yields maximal bad descendants; nesting gives disjointness and coverage, and the good parent gives the 2^n bound. Countability, the summed measure estimate, and boundary conventions are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The induction is valid: restriction supplies H^1 derivatives, the commutator formula gives L^2 data with the stated bounds, and the nested H^2 estimate yields the claimed regularity and constants. Dependency interfaces are consistent.

The unitisation bound, translation-ratio character, Bochner convolution identity, approximate-identity limit, uniqueness and norm-one argument are sound under DC and consistent with the supplied interfaces and Fourier convention.

The cited multiplier rule and test-function density justify the strong equation; ellipticity permits division by a^{nn}, and the pointwise bound yields the claimed boundary-half-ball L² estimate. The H²_loc assumption is redundant for normal-derivative existence but valid.

The chain rule supplies both truncation formulas and global integrability criteria. Local product rules, compact support, and positive-cone density justify the cutoff tests; source-pairing and boundary claims match the supplied interfaces.

The openness, Hausdorff separation, compact-neighbourhood, and descended-operation arguments are valid. The product projection is explicitly proved open, so the quotient-map inference is licensed. No choice principle or A/B-interface conflict arises.

The defining relation gives claim 1; shifting the form by M puts its diagonal values in the stated sector and yields claim 2. Normalization, bounded-operator numerical ranges, and the zero-space convention are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The compact exhaustion, truncation, mollification and support control correctly establish density. Dependency restatements and hypotheses are consistent; empty sets and complex scalars are covered, and both Sobolev consequences follow.

Rellich applies under the assumed AC; bounded test pairings identify the strong subsequential limit with the weak limit, including for complex scalars. The reverse triangle inequality then preserves the unit norm. Dependency uses and edge cases are sound.

The chain rule gives one inclusion; the cited chart and realization lemma give the reverse inclusion for m≥1. The m=0 case is correctly handled by affine curves. Dependency restatements and hypotheses are consistent.

F2 says Lax–Milgram gives existence and uniqueness under the stated hypotheses, but its supplied interface additionally requires Countable Choice, which this item does not assume. The energy estimate itself is valid.
The proof steps and dependency restatements are sound. The normal-form basis, ideal divisibilities, root-chain argument, and exceptional case c=-1/2 establish the stated criterion and consequences.

The local representatives equal the mean-zero oscillations. The embedding and Riesz norm identity bound their L2 norms, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives the uniform BMO bound. In the complex case conjugating the Riesz vector preserves its norm.

The contact transformations give the stated strict residual shifts. Uniform terminal divergence and spatial coercivity yield compact nested superlevel sets, so the finite maximum is attained away from both terminal faces without choice.

The decay, dyadic comparison, ball-average domination and good-set arguments are valid. Dependency restatements, finiteness hypotheses, extended integrals and monotone limits are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The kernel mass calculation, Minkowski bound, representative independence, and John-domain volume estimate are valid. The dependency interfaces support the argument, including null-set and measurability handling.

The cutoff identities, flux bounds, entropy argument and convergence limits are valid under the supplied interfaces. Continuity extends the positive-time identities to endpoint times; no fatal defect found.

The modulus regularization yields the stated distributional inequality; spatial cutoff errors vanish using the uniform L¹ bound, and L¹ continuity supplies both time endpoints. The cited interfaces support the argument.

The gradient and coefficient formulas correctly transform the weak identity. Compactly supported H¹ tests are admissible, cutoff bounds justify global Sobolev transfer, and approximation preserves H¹₀. The dependency interfaces support the argument.

The integration-by-parts signs, Sobolev product rules, derivative commutation, and higher-order commutator bounds are valid. The supplied interfaces justify the L²_loc data and local weak-solution claims on relatively compact subdomains.

The differentiated contour integrals, pointwise closedness argument for domain membership, vanishing scalar integrals, induction, and radius scaling establish both claims. Dependency restatements and sector angles are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The good-lambda absorption, dense-class finiteness, weighted extensions (including A_1), and principal-value convergence argument are sound. Dependency restatements and hypotheses are consistent with the supplied interfaces.

The consistency identity, local measure gluing, inversion on the core, translation invariance, and uniqueness and reciprocal scaling are valid. Dependency restatements and A/B interfaces are consistent; no fatal defect found.

The local bound, semigroup decomposition, submultiplicativity, and exponential comparison establish the claimed estimate. Dependency restatements are consistent, and the zero-space case is handled correctly.

The kernel-annihilation dependency applies exactly; surjectivity gives independent component functionals, and the common-kernel lemma yields unique multipliers. The zero-constraint case and reindexing are handled correctly.

The localisation, finite-cover bounds, decreasing subsequence extraction and limit inequalities are valid. Dependency restatements and choice accounting agree with the supplied interfaces; the initial-trace and dual arguments are sound.

The induction is sound: tangential derivatives preserve zero trace, commutator data lie in L², and the equation recovers higher normal derivatives. The supplied dependency interfaces support the localization and regularity steps.

The frozen-coefficient estimate, doubled-ball interpolation, bounded-overlap covering and hole-filling iteration are valid. Dependency restatements and hypotheses agree with the supplied interfaces; no fatal defect found.

The continuous inversion argument establishes the C_c isometry; simultaneous L^1/L^2 approximation identifies its extension with the Fourier transform. Dependency interfaces, choice hypotheses, quotient notation and A/B interfaces are consistent.
